title: A Bend in the River
author: V. S. Naipaul
description: Salim, a Muslim of Indian descent, buys a shop in a town at a bend of the great river in the interior of a newly independent central African country, and watches the fragile post-colonial order rise and rot under the rule of the Big Man. Naipaul's unnamed town is drawn from Kisangani on the Congo: the river and its choking water hyacinths, the market and the shop, the Big Man's shiny new Domain on the edge of the bush, and the far-off capital from which power and terror flow.

route.summary: Salim drives inland to buy a shop in the half-ruined town at the bend of the river, where the trade of the interior slowly revives after the chaos of independence. The market, the shabby shops, the mix of peoples washed up here, this is the frontier world in which Naipaul watches a new Africa try, and fail, to hold itself together.
route.note: Salim's shop and the market town at the river's bend are drawn from Kisangani, the real city on the upper Congo, left unnamed in the novel; sited there.

route.summary: Down the great river the marchande Zabeth poles her dugout from her secret village to trade at Salim's shop, and up it drifts the water hyacinth, the new weed choking the channels. The river, carrying both commerce and the ever-returning wild, is the book's central presence, indifferent to the human schemes on its banks.
route.note: The great river of the novel is the Congo, on which the town sits and by which the trader-woman Zabeth brings her goods; sited on the river at the town.

route.summary: On the edge of town the Big Man raises the Domain, a gleaming new suburb of villas and a polytechnic meant to embody the modern Africa, where the bright young Ferdinand studies. Naipaul makes the Domain the emblem of a borrowed, hollow modernity, impressive and unreal, already cracking as soon as it is built.
route.note: The Domain, the Big Man's showpiece of model buildings and a new university on the town's edge, is drawn from Mobutu-era development projects and sited beside the river town.

route.summary: Above the town the river breaks into the great rapids that halt navigation, the reason a settlement grew here at all. The falls, thunderous and unchanging, frame the town's whole precarious life, marking the limit where the modern world's boats stop and the deep interior begins.
route.note: The rapids just above the town are the real Boyoma (Stanley) Falls at Kisangani, the head of navigation on the Congo; sited there.

route.summary: From the far-off capital the Big Man's power and cult radiate outward, his portraits, his edicts, his sudden campaigns of nationalisation and terror reaching even this remote town. Naipaul lets the unseen capital stand for the whole arbitrary machinery of the new state, under which Salim's world is at last confiscated and he must flee.
route.note: The distant capital from which the Big Man rules is drawn from Kinshasa, the real seat of Mobutu's power; sited there, far downriver from the town.
